     197: /**
     198:  * ✅ Normaliza "horário" para HH:MM
     199:  */
>>   200: function normalizeHourLike(value) {
     201:   const s0 = String(value ?? "").trim();
     202:   if (!s0) return "";
     203: 
     204:   const s = s0.replace(/\s+/g, "");
     205: 
     206:   const mhx = s.match(/^(\d{1,2})(?:h|hs|hr|hrs)$/i);
     207:   if (mhx) return `${pad2(mhx[1])}:00`;
     208: 
     209:   const mISO = s.match(/^(\d{1,2}):(\d{1,2})(?::(\d{1,2}))?$/);
     210:   if (mISO) return `${pad2(mISO[1])}:${pad2(mISO[2])}`;
     211: 
     212:   const mHm = s.match(/^(\d{3,4})$/);
     213:   if (mHm) {
     214:     const hh = String(mHm[1]).slice(0, -2);
     215:     const mm = String(mHm[1]).slice(-2);
     216:     if (/^\d{1,2}$/.test(hh) && /^\d{2}$/.test(mm)) {
     217:       return `${pad2(hh)}:${mm}`;
     218:     }
     219:   }
     220: 
     221:   const m2 = s.match(/^(\d{1,2})$/);
     222:   if (m2) return `${pad2(m2[1])}:00`;
     223: 
     224:   return s0.trim();
     225: }

     227: function mhxToInt(v) {
     228:   const n = Number(v);
     229:   return Number.isFinite(n) ? n : 0;
     230: }

     232: /**
     233:  * ✅ Bucket "09h", "11h"…
     234:  */
>>   235: function toHourBucket(value) {
     236:   const s = String(value ?? "").trim();
     237:   if (!s || s.toLowerCase() === "todos") return null;
     238: 
     239:   const mh = s.match(/^(\d{1,2})h$/i);
     240:   if (mh) return `${pad2(mhxToInt(mh[1]))}h`;
     241: 
     242:   const m1 = s.match(/^(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})$/);
     243:   if (m1) return `${pad2(mhxToInt(m1[1]))}h`;
     244: 
     245:   const m2 = s.match(/^(\d{1,2})$/);
     246:   if (m2) return `${pad2(mhxToInt(m2[1]))}h`;
     247: 
     248:   const m3 = s.match(/^(\d{1,2}):(\d{2}):(\d{2})$/);
     249:   if (m3) return `${pad2(mhxToInt(m3[1]))}h`;
     250: 
     251:   const m4 = s.match(/^(\d{3,4})$/);
     252:   if (m4) return `${pad2(mhxToInt(String(m4[1]).slice(0, -2)))}h`;
     253: 
     254:   return null;
     255: }

     383: function dedupeDrawsLocal(draws) {
     384:   const arr = Array.isArray(draws) ? draws : [];
     385: 
     386:   const byKey = new Map();
     387:   const order = [];
     388: 
     389:   function score(d) {
     390:     const prizesLen = Array.isArray(d?.prizes) ? d.prizes.length : 0;
     391:     const pc = Number.isFinite(Number(d?.prizesCount))
     392:       ? Number(d.prizesCount)
     393:       : 0;
>>   394:     const hasLogical = !!(d?.ymd && d?.close_hour);
     395:     return prizesLen * 1_000_000 + pc * 1_000 + (hasLogical ? 10 : 0);
     396:   }
     397: 
     398:   for (let i = 0; i < arr.length; i += 1) {
     399:     const raw = arr[i] || {};
     400: 
     401:     const ymd = raw.ymd || normalizeToYMD(raw.date) || "";
>>   402:     const hour = normalizeHourLike(raw.close_hour || raw.closeHour || "");
     403: 
     404:     const lotCode = normalizeLotteryCodeAny(raw);
     405: 
     406:     const drawId = raw.drawId ?? raw.id ?? raw.__name__ ?? null;
     407:     const idStr = drawId != null ? String(drawId) : "";
     408: 
     409:     const hasLogical = !!(ymd && hour);
     410: 
     411:     const key = hasLogical
     412:       ? lotCode
     413:         ? `${ymd}__${hour}__${lotCode}`
     414:         : `${ymd}__${hour}`
     415:       : `id__${idStr || `idx_${i}`}`;
     416: 
     417:     const normalized = {
     418:       ...raw,
     419:       ymd: ymd || raw.ymd || null,
>>   420:       close_hour: hour || raw.close_hour || raw.closeHour || "",
>>   421:       closeHour: hour || raw.closeHour || raw.close_hour || "",
     422:       lottery_code: lotCode || raw.lottery_code || raw.lotteryCode || null,
     423:       drawId: raw.drawId || raw.id || raw.__name__ || null,
     424:       id: raw.id || raw.drawId || raw.__name__ || null,
     425:     };
     426: 
     427:     if (!byKey.has(key)) {
     428:       byKey.set(key, normalized);
     429:       order.push(key);
     430:       continue;
     431:     }
     432: 
     433:     const prev = byKey.get(key);
     434:     if (score(normalized) > score(prev)) {
     435:       byKey.set(key, normalized);
     436:     }
     437:   }
     438: 
>>   439:   return order.map((k) => byKey.get(k)).filter(Boolean);
     440: }

     442: async function mapWithConcurrency(items, limitN, mapper) {
     443:   const arr = Array.isArray(items) ? items : [];
     444:   const concurrency = Math.max(1, Number(limitN) || 6);
     445:   const results = new Array(arr.length);
     446:   let idx = 0;
     447: 
     448:   async function worker() {
     449:     while (true) {
     450:       const current = idx;
     451:       idx += 1;
     452:       if (current >= arr.length) break;
     453:       results[current] = await mapper(arr[current], current);
     454:     }
     455:   }
     456: 
     457:   await Promise.all(
     458:     Array.from({ length: Math.min(concurrency, arr.length) }, () => worker())
     459:   );
     460:   return results;
     461: }

      35: async function mapWithConcurrency(items, concurrency, mapper) {
      36:   const arr = Array.isArray(items) ? items : [];
      37:   const out = new Array(arr.length);
      38:   let index = 0;
      39: 
      40:   async function worker() {
      41:     while (index < arr.length) {
      42:       const i = index++;
      43:       out[i] = await mapper(arr[i], i);
      44:     }
      45:   }
      46: 
      47:   await Promise.all(
      48:     Array.from({ length: Math.min(concurrency, arr.length) }, worker)
      49:   );
      50: 
      51:   return out;
      52: }

    6991:         sparseSnapshotTree.value = data;
    6992:         sparseSnapshotTree.children.clear();
    6993:     }

    6996:     }

    7000:             sparseSnapshotTree.children.set(childKey, newSparseSnapshotTree());

    7003:         path = pathPopFront(path);
    7004:         sparseSnapshotTreeRemember(child, path, data);
    7005:     }
    7006: }
    7007: /**
    7008:  * Purge the data at path from the cache.
    7009:  *
>>  7010:  * @param path - Path to look up snapshot for.
    7011:  * @returns True if this node should now be removed.
    7012:  */
    7013: function sparseSnapshotTreeForget(sparseSnapshotTree, path) {
    7014:     if (pathIsEmpty(path)) {
    7015:         sparseSnapshotTree.value = null;
    7016:         sparseSnapshotTree.children.clear();
    7017:         return true;
    7018:     }
    7019:     else {
    7020:         if (sparseSnapshotTree.value !== null) {
    7021:             if (sparseSnapshotTree.value.isLeafNode()) {
    7022:                 // We're trying to forget a node that doesn't exist
    7023:                 return false;
    7024:             }
    7025:             else {
    7026:                 const value = sparseSnapshotTree.value;
    7027:                 sparseSnapshotTree.value = null;
    7028:                 value.forEachChild(PRIORITY_INDEX, (key, tree) => {
    7029:                     sparseSnapshotTreeRemember(sparseSnapshotTree, new Path(key), tree);
    7030:                 });
    7031:                 return sparseSnapshotTreeForget(sparseSnapshotTree, path);
    7032:             }
    7033:         }
    7034:         else if (sparseSnapshotTree.children.size > 0) {
    7035:             const childKey = pathGetFront(path);
    7036:             path = pathPopFront(path);
    7037:             if (sparseSnapshotTree.children.has(childKey)) {
    7038:                 const safeToRemove = sparseSnapshotTreeForget(sparseSnapshotTree.children.get(childKey), path);
    7039:                 if (safeToRemove) {
    7040:                     sparseSnapshotTree.children.delete(childKey);
    7041:                 }
    7042:             }
    7043:             return sparseSnapshotTree.children.size === 0;
    7044:         }
    7045:         else {
    7046:             return true;
    7047:         }
    7048:     }
    7049: }

    6972: function newSparseSnapshotTree() {
    6973:     return {

    6978: /**
    6979:  * Stores the given node at the specified path. If there is already a node
    6980:  * at a shallower path, it merges the new data into that snapshot node.
    6981:  *
>>  6982:  * @param path - Path to look up snapshot for.
    6983:  * @param data - The new data, or null.
    6984:  */
    6985: function sparseSnapshotTreeRemember(sparseSnapshotTree, path, data) {
    6986:     if (pathIsEmpty(path)) {
    6987:         sparseSnapshotTree.value = data;
    6988:         sparseSnapshotTree.children.clear();
    6989:     }
    6990:     else if (sparseSnapshotTree.value !== null) {
    6991:         sparseSnapshotTree.value = sparseSnapshotTree.value.updateChild(path, data);
    6992:     }
    6993:     else {
    6994:         const childKey = pathGetFront(path);
    6995:         if (!sparseSnapshotTree.children.has(childKey)) {
    6996:             sparseSnapshotTree.children.set(childKey, newSparseSnapshotTree());
    6997:         }
    6998:         const child = sparseSnapshotTree.children.get(childKey);
    6999:         path = pathPopFront(path);
    7000:         sparseSnapshotTreeRemember(child, path, data);
    7001:     }
    7002: }
    7003: /**
    7004:  * Purge the data at path from the cache.
    7005:  *
>>  7006:  * @param path - Path to look up snapshot for.
    7007:  * @returns True if this node should now be removed.
    7008:  */
    7009: function sparseSnapshotTreeForget(sparseSnapshotTree, path) {
    7010:     if (pathIsEmpty(path)) {
    7011:         sparseSnapshotTree.value = null;
    7012:         sparseSnapshotTree.children.clear();
    7013:         return true;
    7014:     }
    7015:     else {
    7016:         if (sparseSnapshotTree.value !== null) {
    7017:             if (sparseSnapshotTree.value.isLeafNode()) {
    7018:                 // We're trying to forget a node that doesn't exist
    7019:                 return false;
    7020:             }
    7021:             else {
    7022:                 const value = sparseSnapshotTree.value;
    7023:                 sparseSnapshotTree.value = null;
    7024:                 value.forEachChild(PRIORITY_INDEX, (key, tree) => {
    7025:                     sparseSnapshotTreeRemember(sparseSnapshotTree, new Path(key), tree);
    7026:                 });
    7027:                 return sparseSnapshotTreeForget(sparseSnapshotTree, path);
    7028:             }
    7029:         }
    7030:         else if (sparseSnapshotTree.children.size > 0) {
    7031:             const childKey = pathGetFront(path);
    7032:             path = pathPopFront(path);
    7033:             if (sparseSnapshotTree.children.has(childKey)) {
    7034:                 const safeToRemove = sparseSnapshotTreeForget(sparseSnapshotTree.children.get(childKey), path);
    7035:                 if (safeToRemove) {
    7036:                     sparseSnapshotTree.children.delete(childKey);
    7037:                 }
    7038:             }
    7039:             return sparseSnapshotTree.children.size === 0;
    7040:         }
    7041:         else {
    7042:             return true;
    7043:         }
    7044:     }
    7045: }
    7046: /**
    7047:  * Recursively iterates through all of the stored tree and calls the
    7048:  * callback on each one.
    7049:  *
>>  7050:  * @param prefixPath - Path to look up node for.
    7051:  * @param func - The function to invoke for each tree.
    7052:  */
    7053: function sparseSnapshotTreeForEachTree(sparseSnapshotTree, prefixPath, func) {
    7054:     if (sparseSnapshotTree.value !== null) {
    7055:         func(prefixPath, sparseSnapshotTree.value);
    7056:     }
    7057:     else {
    7058:         sparseSnapshotTreeForEachChild(sparseSnapshotTree, (key, tree) => {
    7059:             const path = new Path(prefixPath.toString() + '/' + key);
    7060:             sparseSnapshotTreeForEachTree(tree, path, func);
    7061:         });
    7062:     }
    7063: }
    7064: /**
    7065:  * Iterates through each immediate child and triggers the callback.
    7066:  * Only seems to be used in tests.
    7067:  *
    7068:  * @param func - The function to invoke for each child.
    7069:  */
    7070: function sparseSnapshotTreeForEachChild(sparseSnapshotTree, func) {
    7071:     sparseSnapshotTree.children.forEach((tree, key) => {
    7072:         func(key, tree);

    6990: /**
    6991:  * Stores the given node at the specified path. If there is already a node
    6992:  * at a shallower path, it merges the new data into that snapshot node.
    6993:  *
>>  6994:  * @param path - Path to look up snapshot for.
    6995:  * @param data - The new data, or null.
    6996:  */
    6997: function sparseSnapshotTreeRemember(sparseSnapshotTree, path, data) {
    6998:     if (pathIsEmpty(path)) {
    6999:         sparseSnapshotTree.value = data;
    7000:         sparseSnapshotTree.children.clear();
    7001:     }
    7002:     else if (sparseSnapshotTree.value !== null) {
    7003:         sparseSnapshotTree.value = sparseSnapshotTree.value.updateChild(path, data);
    7004:     }
    7005:     else {
    7006:         const childKey = pathGetFront(path);
    7007:         if (!sparseSnapshotTree.children.has(childKey)) {
    7008:             sparseSnapshotTree.children.set(childKey, newSparseSnapshotTree());
    7009:         }
    7010:         const child = sparseSnapshotTree.children.get(childKey);
    7011:         path = pathPopFront(path);
    7012:         sparseSnapshotTreeRemember(child, path, data);
    7013:     }
    7014: }
    7015: /**
    7016:  * Purge the data at path from the cache.
    7017:  *
>>  7018:  * @param path - Path to look up snapshot for.
    7019:  * @returns True if this node should now be removed.
    7020:  */
    7021: function sparseSnapshotTreeForget(sparseSnapshotTree, path) {
    7022:     if (pathIsEmpty(path)) {
    7023:         sparseSnapshotTree.value = null;
    7024:         sparseSnapshotTree.children.clear();
    7025:         return true;
    7026:     }
    7027:     else {
    7028:         if (sparseSnapshotTree.value !== null) {
    7029:             if (sparseSnapshotTree.value.isLeafNode()) {
    7030:                 // We're trying to forget a node that doesn't exist
    7031:                 return false;
    7032:             }
    7033:             else {
    7034:                 const value = sparseSnapshotTree.value;
    7035:                 sparseSnapshotTree.value = null;
    7036:                 value.forEachChild(PRIORITY_INDEX, (key, tree) => {
    7037:                     sparseSnapshotTreeRemember(sparseSnapshotTree, new Path(key), tree);
    7038:                 });
    7039:                 return sparseSnapshotTreeForget(sparseSnapshotTree, path);
    7040:             }
    7041:         }
    7042:         else if (sparseSnapshotTree.children.size > 0) {
    7043:             const childKey = pathGetFront(path);
    7044:             path = pathPopFront(path);
    7045:             if (sparseSnapshotTree.children.has(childKey)) {
    7046:                 const safeToRemove = sparseSnapshotTreeForget(sparseSnapshotTree.children.get(childKey), path);
    7047:                 if (safeToRemove) {
    7048:                     sparseSnapshotTree.children.delete(childKey);
    7049:                 }
    7050:             }
    7051:             return sparseSnapshotTree.children.size === 0;
    7052:         }
    7053:         else {
    7054:             return true;
    7055:         }
    7056:     }
    7057: }
    7058: /**
    7059:  * Recursively iterates through all of the stored tree and calls the
    7060:  * callback on each one.

>>  7062:  * @param prefixPath - Path to look up node for.

    9143: /**
    9144:  * A view represents a specific location and query that has 1 or more event registrations.
    9145:  *
    9146:  * It does several things:
    9147:  *  - Maintains the list of event registrations for this location/query.
    9148:  *  - Maintains a cache of the data visible for this location/query.
    9149:  *  - Applies new operations (via applyOperation), updates the cache, and based on the event
    9150:  *    registrations returns the set of events to be raised.
    9151:  */
    9152: class View {

    9161:         const initialEventCache = initialViewCache.eventCache;
>>  9162:         // Don't filter server node with other filter than index, wait for tagged listen
>>  9163:         const serverSnap = indexFilter.updateFullNode(ChildrenNode.EMPTY_NODE, initialServerCache.getNode(), null);
>>  9164:         const eventSnap = filter.updateFullNode(ChildrenNode.EMPTY_NODE, initialEventCache.getNode(), null);
>>  9165:         const newServerCache = new CacheNode(serverSnap, initialServerCache.isFullyInitialized(), indexFilter.filtersNodes());
>>  9166:         const newEventCache = new CacheNode(eventSnap, initialEventCache.isFullyInitialized(), filter.filtersNodes());
    9167:         this.viewCache_ = newViewCache(newEventCache, newServerCache);
    9168:         this.eventGenerator_ = new EventGenerator(this.query_);
    9169:     }
    9170:     get query() {
    9171:         return this.query_;
    9172:     }
    9173: }

    6995:     if (pathIsEmpty(path)) {
    6996:         sparseSnapshotTree.value = data;
    6997:         sparseSnapshotTree.children.clear();
    6998:     }
    6999:     else if (sparseSnapshotTree.value !== null) {
    7000:         sparseSnapshotTree.value = sparseSnapshotTree.value.updateChild(path, data);
    7001:     }
    7002:     else {
    7003:         const childKey = pathGetFront(path);
    7004:         if (!sparseSnapshotTree.children.has(childKey)) {
    7005:             sparseSnapshotTree.children.set(childKey, newSparseSnapshotTree());
    7006:         }
    7007:         const child = sparseSnapshotTree.children.get(childKey);
    7008:         path = pathPopFront(path);
    7009:         sparseSnapshotTreeRemember(child, path, data);
    7010:     }
    7011: }
    7012: /**
    7013:  * Purge the data at path from the cache.
    7014:  *
>>  7015:  * @param path - Path to look up snapshot for.
    7016:  * @returns True if this node should now be removed.
    7017:  */
    7018: function sparseSnapshotTreeForget(sparseSnapshotTree, path) {
    7019:     if (pathIsEmpty(path)) {
    7020:         sparseSnapshotTree.value = null;
    7021:         sparseSnapshotTree.children.clear();
    7022:         return true;
    7023:     }
    7024:     else {
    7025:         if (sparseSnapshotTree.value !== null) {
    7026:             if (sparseSnapshotTree.value.isLeafNode()) {
    7027:                 // We're trying to forget a node that doesn't exist
    7028:                 return false;
    7029:             }
    7030:             else {
    7031:                 const value = sparseSnapshotTree.value;
    7032:                 sparseSnapshotTree.value = null;
    7033:                 value.forEachChild(PRIORITY_INDEX, (key, tree) => {
    7034:                     sparseSnapshotTreeRemember(sparseSnapshotTree, new Path(key), tree);
    7035:                 });
    7036:                 return sparseSnapshotTreeForget(sparseSnapshotTree, path);
    7037:             }
    7038:         }
    7039:         else if (sparseSnapshotTree.children.size > 0) {
    7040:             const childKey = pathGetFront(path);
    7041:             path = pathPopFront(path);
    7042:             if (sparseSnapshotTree.children.has(childKey)) {
    7043:                 const safeToRemove = sparseSnapshotTreeForget(sparseSnapshotTree.children.get(childKey), path);
    7044:                 if (safeToRemove) {
    7045:                     sparseSnapshotTree.children.delete(childKey);
    7046:                 }
    7047:             }
    7048:             return sparseSnapshotTree.children.size === 0;
    7049:         }
    7050:         else {
    7051:             return true;
    7052:         }
    7053:     }
    7054: }

    6037:     updateChild(snap, key, newChild, affectedPath, source, optChangeAccumulator) {
    6038:         assert(snap.isIndexed(this.index_), 'A node must be indexed if only a child is updated');
    6039:         const oldChild = snap.getImmediateChild(key);
    6040:         // Check if anything actually changed.
    6041:         if (oldChild.getChild(affectedPath).equals(newChild.getChild(affectedPath))) {
    6042:             // There's an edge case where a child can enter or leave the view because affectedPath was set to null.
    6043:             // In this case, affectedPath will appear null in both the old and new snapshots.  So we need
    6044:             // to avoid treating these cases as "nothing changed."
    6045:             if (oldChild.isEmpty() === newChild.isEmpty()) {
    6046:                 // Nothing changed.
    6047:                 // This assert should be valid, but it's expensive (can dominate perf testing) so don't actually do it.
    6048:                 //assert(oldChild.equals(newChild), 'Old and new snapshots should be equal.');
    6049:                 return snap;
    6050:             }
    6051:         }
    6052:         if (optChangeAccumulator != null) {
    6053:             if (newChild.isEmpty()) {
    6054:                 if (snap.hasChild(key)) {
    6055:                     optChangeAccumulator.trackChildChange(changeChildRemoved(key, oldChild));
    6056:                 }
    6057:                 else {
    6058:                     assert(snap.isLeafNode(), 'A child remove without an old child only makes sense on a leaf node');

    6976: function newSparseSnapshotTree() {

    6982: /**
    6983:  * Stores the given node at the specified path. If there is already a node
    6984:  * at a shallower path, it merges the new data into that snapshot node.
    6985:  *
>>  6986:  * @param path - Path to look up snapshot for.
    6987:  * @param data - The new data, or null.
    6988:  */
    6989: function sparseSnapshotTreeRemember(sparseSnapshotTree, path, data) {
    6990:     if (pathIsEmpty(path)) {
    6991:         sparseSnapshotTree.value = data;
    6992:         sparseSnapshotTree.children.clear();
    6993:     }
    6994:     else if (sparseSnapshotTree.value !== null) {
    6995:         sparseSnapshotTree.value = sparseSnapshotTree.value.updateChild(path, data);
    6996:     }
    6997:     else {
    6998:         const childKey = pathGetFront(path);
    6999:         if (!sparseSnapshotTree.children.has(childKey)) {
    7000:             sparseSnapshotTree.children.set(childKey, newSparseSnapshotTree());
    7001:         }
    7002:         const child = sparseSnapshotTree.children.get(childKey);
    7003:         path = pathPopFront(path);
    7004:         sparseSnapshotTreeRemember(child, path, data);
    7005:     }
    7006: }
    7007: /**
    7008:  * Purge the data at path from the cache.
    7009:  *
>>  7010:  * @param path - Path to look up snapshot for.
    7011:  * @returns True if this node should now be removed.
    7012:  */
    7013: function sparseSnapshotTreeForget(sparseSnapshotTree, path) {
    7014:     if (pathIsEmpty(path)) {
    7015:         sparseSnapshotTree.value = null;
    7016:         sparseSnapshotTree.children.clear();
    7017:         return true;
    7018:     }
    7019:     else {
    7020:         if (sparseSnapshotTree.value !== null) {
    7021:             if (sparseSnapshotTree.value.isLeafNode()) {
    7022:                 // We're trying to forget a node that doesn't exist
    7023:                 return false;
    7024:             }
    7025:             else {
    7026:                 const value = sparseSnapshotTree.value;
    7027:                 sparseSnapshotTree.value = null;
    7028:                 value.forEachChild(PRIORITY_INDEX, (key, tree) => {
    7029:                     sparseSnapshotTreeRemember(sparseSnapshotTree, new Path(key), tree);
    7030:                 });
    7031:                 return sparseSnapshotTreeForget(sparseSnapshotTree, path);
    7032:             }
    7033:         }
    7034:         else if (sparseSnapshotTree.children.size > 0) {
    7035:             const childKey = pathGetFront(path);
    7036:             path = pathPopFront(path);
    7037:             if (sparseSnapshotTree.children.has(childKey)) {
    7038:                 const safeToRemove = sparseSnapshotTreeForget(sparseSnapshotTree.children.get(childKey), path);
    7039:                 if (safeToRemove) {
    7040:                     sparseSnapshotTree.children.delete(childKey);
    7041:                 }
    7042:             }
    7043:             return sparseSnapshotTree.children.size === 0;
    7044:         }
    7045:         else {
    7046:             return true;
    7047:         }
    7048:     }
    7049: }
    7050: /**
    7051:  * Recursively iterates through all of the stored tree and calls the
    7052:  * callback on each one.
    7053:  *
>>  7054:  * @param prefixPath - Path to look up node for.
    7055:  * @param func - The function to invoke for each tree.
    7056:  */
    7057: function sparseSnapshotTreeForEachTree(sparseSnapshotTree, prefixPath, func) {
    7058:     if (sparseSnapshotTree.value !== null) {
    7059:         func(prefixPath, sparseSnapshotTree.value);
    7060:     }
    7061:     else {
    7062:         sparseSnapshotTreeForEachChild(sparseSnapshotTree, (key, tree) => {
    7063:             const path = new Path(prefixPath.toString() + '/' + key);
    7064:             sparseSnapshotTreeForEachTree(tree, path, func);
    7065:         });
    7066:     }
    7067: }
    7068: /**
    7069:  * Iterates through each immediate child and triggers the callback.

    7074: function sparseSnapshotTreeForEachChild(sparseSnapshotTree, func) {
    7075:     sparseSnapshotTree.children.forEach((tree, key) => {

   11908: /**
   11909:  * Stores the given node at the specified path. If there is already a node
   11910:  * at a shallower path, it merges the new data into that snapshot node.
   11911:  *
>> 11912:  * @param path - Path to look up snapshot for.
   11913:  * @param data - The new data, or null.
   11914:  */
   11915: function sparseSnapshotTreeRemember(sparseSnapshotTree, path, data) {
   11916:     if (pathIsEmpty(path)) {
   11917:         sparseSnapshotTree.value = data;
   11918:         sparseSnapshotTree.children.clear();
   11919:     }
   11920:     else if (sparseSnapshotTree.value !== null) {
   11921:         sparseSnapshotTree.value = sparseSnapshotTree.value.updateChild(path, data);
   11922:     }
   11923:     else {
   11924:         const childKey = pathGetFront(path);
   11925:         if (!sparseSnapshotTree.children.has(childKey)) {
   11926:             sparseSnapshotTree.children.set(childKey, newSparseSnapshotTree());
   11927:         }
   11928:         const child = sparseSnapshotTree.children.get(childKey);
   11929:         path = pathPopFront(path);
   11930:         sparseSnapshotTreeRemember(child, path, data);
   11931:     }
   11932: }
   11933: /**
   11934:  * Purge the data at path from the cache.
   11935:  *
>> 11936:  * @param path - Path to look up snapshot for.
   11937:  * @returns True if this node should now be removed.
   11938:  */
   11939: function sparseSnapshotTreeForget(sparseSnapshotTree, path) {
   11940:     if (pathIsEmpty(path)) {
   11941:         sparseSnapshotTree.value = null;
   11942:         sparseSnapshotTree.children.clear();
   11943:         return true;
   11944:     }
   11945:     else {
   11946:         if (sparseSnapshotTree.value !== null) {
   11947:             if (sparseSnapshotTree.value.isLeafNode()) {
   11948:                 // We're trying to forget a node that doesn't exist
   11949:                 return false;
   11950:             }
   11951:             else {
   11952:                 const value = sparseSnapshotTree.value;
   11953:                 sparseSnapshotTree.value = null;
   11954:                 value.forEachChild(PRIORITY_INDEX, (key, tree) => {
   11955:                     sparseSnapshotTreeRemember(sparseSnapshotTree, new Path(key), tree);
   11956:                 });
   11957:                 return sparseSnapshotTreeForget(sparseSnapshotTree, path);
   11958:             }
   11959:         }
   11960:         else if (sparseSnapshotTree.children.size > 0) {
   11961:             const childKey = pathGetFront(path);
   11962:             path = pathPopFront(path);
   11963:             if (sparseSnapshotTree.children.has(childKey)) {
   11964:                 const safeToRemove = sparseSnapshotTreeForget(sparseSnapshotTree.children.get(childKey), path);
   11965:                 if (safeToRemove) {
   11966:                     sparseSnapshotTree.children.delete(childKey);
   11967:                 }
   11968:             }
   11969:             return sparseSnapshotTree.children.size === 0;
   11970:         }
   11971:         else {
   11972:             return true;
   11973:         }
   11974:     }
   11975: }

       8: const ansi = new RegExp('\x1b(?:\\[(?:\\d+[ABCDEFGJKSTm]|\\d+;\\d+[Hfm]|' +
       9:     '\\d+;\\d+;\\d+m|6n|s|u|\\?25[lh])|\\w)', 'g');
      10: export function stripAnsi(str) {
      11:     return str.replace(ansi, '');
      12: }
      13: export function wrap(str, width) {
      14:     const [start, end] = str.match(ansi) || ['', ''];
      15:     str = stripAnsi(str);
      16:     let wrapped = '';
      17:     for (let i = 0; i < str.length; i++) {
      18:         if (i !== 0 && (i % width) === 0) {
      19:             wrapped += '\n';
      20:         }
      21:         wrapped += str.charAt(i);
      22:     }
      23:     if (start && end) {
      24:         wrapped = `${start}${wrapped}${end}`;
      25:     }
      26:     return wrapped;
      27: }

     214: /**
     215:  * Validates that a string is a valid web URL.
     216:  *
     217:  * @param urlStr - The string to validate.
     218:  * @returns Whether the string is valid web URL or not.
     219:  */
     220: function isURL(urlStr) {
     221:     if (typeof urlStr !== 'string') {
     222:         return false;
     223:     }
>>   224:     // Lookup illegal characters.
     225:     const re = /[^a-z0-9:/?#[\]@!$&'()*+,;=.\-_~%]/i;
     226:     if (re.test(urlStr)) {
     227:         return false;
     228:     }
     229:     try {
     230:         const uri = url.parse(urlStr);
     231:         const scheme = uri.protocol;
     232:         const slashes = uri.slashes;
     233:         const hostname = uri.hostname;
     234:         const pathname = uri.pathname;
     235:         if ((scheme !== 'http:' && scheme !== 'https:') || !slashes) {
     236:             return false;
     237:         }
     238:         // Validate hostname: Can contain letters, numbers, underscore and dashes separated by a dot.
     239:         // Each zone must not start with a hyphen or underscore.
     240:         if (!hostname || !/^[a-zA-Z0-9]+[\w-]*([.]?[a-zA-Z0-9]+[\w-]*)*$/.test(hostname)) {
     241:             return false;
     242:         }
     243:         // Allow for pathnames: (/chars+)*/?
     244:         // Where chars can be a combination of: a-z A-Z 0-9 - _ . ~ ! $ & ' ( ) * + , ; = : @ %
     245:         const pathnameRe = /^(\/[\w\-.~!$'()*+,;=:@%]+)*\/?$/;
     246:         // Validate pathname.
     247:         if (pathname &&
     248:             pathname !== '/' &&
     249:             !pathnameRe.test(pathname)) {
     250:             return false;
     251:         }
     252:         // Allow any query string and hash as long as no invalid character is used.
     253:     }
     254:     catch (e) {
     255:         return false;
     256:     }
     257:     return true;
     258: }

     142:                     errorInfo = decodedDetail;

     144:             }
     145:             catch (err) {
     146:                 // cannot decode detail, likely because of the unknown type - just skip it
     147:             }
     148:         }

     150:             code: status.code,
     151:             message: status.message,
     152:             statusDetails: details,
     153:             reason: errorInfo === null || errorInfo === void 0 ? void 0 : errorInfo.reason,
     154:             domain: errorInfo === null || errorInfo === void 0 ? void 0 : errorInfo.domain,
     155:             errorInfoMetadata: errorInfo === null || errorInfo === void 0 ? void 0 : errorInfo.metadata,
     156:         };
     157:         return result;

     243: // Override the protobuf json's the http rules.
     244: function overrideHttpRules(httpRules, protoJson) {
     245:     for (const rule of httpRules) {
     246:         if (!rule.selector) {
     247:             continue;
     248:         }
>>   249:         const rpc = protoJson.lookup(rule.selector);

     251:         // We could reconsider if we have the use case later.
     252:         if (!rpc || !rpc.parsedOptions) {
     253:             continue;
     254:         }
     255:         for (const item of rpc.parsedOptions) {
     256:             if (!(httpOptionName in item)) {
     257:                 continue;
     258:             }
     259:             const httpOptions = item[httpOptionName];
     260:             for (const httpMethod in httpOptions) {
     261:                 if (httpMethod in rule) {
     262:                     if (httpMethod === 'additional_bindings') {
     263:                         continue;
     264:                     }
     265:                     httpOptions[httpMethod] =
     266:                         rule[httpMethod];
     267:                 }
     268:                 if (rule.additional_bindings) {
     269:                     httpOptions['additional_bindings'] = !httpOptions['additional_bindings']
     270:                         ? []
     271:                         : Array.isArray(httpOptions['additional_bindings'])
     272:                             ? httpOptions['additional_bindings']
     273:                             : [httpOptions['additional_bindings']];
     274:                     // Make the additional_binding to be an array if it is not.
     275:                     httpOptions['additional_bindings'].push(...rule.additional_bindings);
     276:                 }
     277:             }
     278:         }
     279:     }

      66:  * UNIVERSAL 18-22, 25-30 Character string types
      67:  * UNIVERSAL 23-24 Time types
      68:  *
      69:  * The length of an ASN.1 structure is specified after the tag identifier.
      70:  * There is a definite form and an indefinite form. The indefinite form may
      71:  * be used if the encoding is constructed and not all immediately available.
      72:  * The indefinite form is encoded using a length byte with only the 8th bit
      73:  * set. The end of the constructed object is marked using end-of-contents
      74:  * octets (two zero bytes).
      75:  *
>>    76:  * The definite form looks like this:
      77:  *
      78:  * The length may take up 1 or more bytes, it depends on the length of the
      79:  * value of the ASN.1 structure. DER encoding requires that if the ASN.1
      80:  * structure has a value that has a length greater than 127, more than 1 byte
      81:  * will be used to store its length, otherwise just one byte will be used.
      82:  * This is strict.
      83:  *
      84:  * In the case that the length of the ASN.1 value is less than 127, 1 octet
      85:  * (byte) is used to store the "short form" length. The 8th bit has a value of
      86:  * 0 indicating the length is "short form" and not "long form" and bits 7-1
      87:  * give the length of the data. (The 8th bit is the left-most, most significant
      88:  * bit: also known as big endian or network format).
      89:  *
      90:  * In the case that the length of the ASN.1 value is greater than 127, 2 to
      91:  * 127 octets (bytes) are used to store the "long form" length. The first
      92:  * byte's 8th bit is set to 1 to indicate the length is "long form." Bits 7-1
      93:  * give the number of additional octets. All following octets are in base 256
      94:  * with the most significant digit first (typical big-endian binary unsigned
      95:  * integer storage). So, for instance, if the length of a value was 257, the
      96:  * first byte would be set to:
      97:  *
      98:  * 10000010 = 130 = 0x82.
      99:  *
     100:  * This indicates there are 2 octets (base 256) for the length. The second and
     101:  * third bytes (the octets just mentioned) would store the length in base 256:
     102:  *
     103:  * octet 2: 00000001 = 1 * 256^1 = 256
     104:  * octet 3: 00000001 = 1 * 256^0 = 1
     105:  * total = 257
     106:  *
     107:  * The algorithm for converting a js integer value of 257 to base-256 is:
     108:  *
     109:  * var value = 257;

--- LINHAS 13 A 57 ---
      13: //
      14: // THE SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, EXPRESS
      15: // OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE WARRANTIES OF
      16: // MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND NONINFRINGEMENT. IN
      17: // NO EVENT SHALL THE AUTHORS OR COPYRIGHT HOLDERS BE LIABLE FOR ANY CLAIM,
      18: // DAMAGES OR OTHER LIABILITY, WHETHER IN AN ACTION OF CONTRACT, TORT OR
      19: // OTHERWISE, ARISING FROM, OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THE SOFTWARE OR THE
      20: // USE OR OTHER DEALINGS IN THE SOFTWARE.
      21: 
      22: // a transform stream is a readable/writable stream where you do
>>    23: // something with the data.  Sometimes it's called a "filter",
      24: // but that's not a great name for it, since that implies a thing where
      25: // some bits pass through, and others are simply ignored.  (That would
      26: // be a valid example of a transform, of course.)
      27: //
      28: // While the output is causally related to the input, it's not a
      29: // necessarily symmetric or synchronous transformation.  For example,
      30: // a zlib stream might take multiple plain-text writes(), and then
      31: // emit a single compressed chunk some time in the future.
      32: //
      33: // Here's how this works:
      34: //
      35: // The Transform stream has all the aspects of the readable and writable
      36: // stream classes.  When you write(chunk), that calls _write(chunk,cb)
      37: // internally, and returns false if there's a lot of pending writes
      38: // buffered up.  When you call read(), that calls _read(n) until
      39: // there's enough pending readable data buffered up.
      40: //
      41: // In a transform stream, the written data is placed in a buffer.  When
      42: // _read(n) is called, it transforms the queued up data, calling the
      43: // buffered _write cb's as it consumes chunks.  If consuming a single
      44: // written chunk would result in multiple output chunks, then the first
      45: // outputted bit calls the readcb, and subsequent chunks just go into
      46: // the read buffer, and will cause it to emit 'readable' if necessary.
      47: //
      48: // This way, back-pressure is actually determined by the reading side,
      49: // since _read has to be called to start processing a new chunk.  However,
      50: // a pathological inflate type of transform can cause excessive buffering
      51: // here.  For example, imagine a stream where every byte of input is
      52: // interpreted as an integer from 0-255, and then results in that many
      53: // bytes of output.  Writing the 4 bytes {ff,ff,ff,ff} would result in
      54: // 1kb of data being output.  In this case, you could write a very small
      55: // amount of input, and end up with a very large amount of output.  In
      56: // such a pathological inflating mechanism, there'd be no way to tell
      57: // the system to stop doing the transform.  A single 4MB write could

     512: async function mapWithConcurrency(items, limitN, mapper) {
     513:   const arr = Array.isArray(items) ? items : [];
     514:   const concurrency = Math.max(1, Number(limitN) || 6);
     515:   const results = new Array(arr.length);
     516:   let idx = 0;
     517: 
     518:   async function worker() {
     519:     while (true) {
     520:       const current = idx;
     521:       idx += 1;
     522:       if (current >= arr.length) break;
     523:       results[current] = await mapper(arr[current], current);
     524:     }
     525:   }
     526: 
     527:   await Promise.all(
     528:     Array.from({ length: Math.min(concurrency, arr.length) }, () => worker())
     529:   );
     530:   return results;

     181: function pickLogFile({ kind, lottery, start, end }) {

     192:     `^${kind}-${lot}-\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}_to_\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}\\.json$`,
     193:     "i"
     194:   );

>>   197:     .filter((f) => baseRe.test(f))

     200:         new RegExp(`^${kind}-${lot}-(\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2})_to_(\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2})\\.json$`, "i")
     201:       );
     202:       const fStart = m?.[1] || "";
     203:       const fEnd = m?.[2] || "";

     205:       return { f, full, fStart, fEnd, mtimeMs: statMtimeMsSafe(full) };
     206:     });
     207:

>>   211:   const exact = candidates.filter((c) => c.fStart === s && c.fEnd === e);

     214:     return exact[0].full;
     215:   }
     216: 
     217:   // 2) fallback: mais recente (do lottery)
     218:   candidates.sort((a, b) => b.mtimeMs - a.mtimeMs);
     219:   return candidates[0].full;
     220: }

     858: function mergeAndDedupDraws(arrays, lotteryKey) {
     859:   const map = new Map();

     861:   for (const a of arrays) {
     862:     const list = Array.isArray(a) ? a : [];

     872:

     875:       } else {
     876:         // se duplicado, preferir o que tiver mais prizes preenchidos
     877:         const prev = map.get(key);
     878:         const prevCount = countPrizesInDraw(prev);
     879:         const curCount = countPrizesInDraw(d);
     880:         if (curCount > prevCount) map.set(key, d);
     881:       }
     882:     }
     883:   }
     884: 
     885:   return Array.from(map.values());
     886: }

      62: function normalizeHH(raw) {
      63:   const s = safeStr(raw);
      64:   if (!s) return null;
      65:   const m = s.match(/(\d{1,2})/);
      66:   if (!m) return null;
      67:   const hh = Number(m[1]);

      69:   return pad2(hh);

      76:  * - mantém ordem: baseMin0 (0,+1,+2,-1,-2), depois baseMin9 (9,+1,+2,-1,-2)

      92:     }
      93:   }
